findings.governingReading: Taiga demands that her “Disciple Number One,” Illya, be brought in.
findings.explanation: Senior student replaces the numbered Tiger Dojo title and falsely implies seniority.

findings.governingReading: Taiga guesses whether Illya and Leysritt form a boke-and-tsukkomi comedy pair.
findings.explanation: Straight man and foil fails to name the comic instigator and makes both roles sound like counterparts to someone else.

findings.highlight: Then is she off having a fun time with Shirou on her canopy bed right now?
findings.evidenceJa: そこまでお金持ちだったのか
findings.governingReading: The original Japanese proceeds directly from Taiga realizing Illya is rich to her jealous outburst; it has no ghentai conditional dialogue block.
findings.explanation: mirror moon inserts four conditional speeches about Shirou, a canopy-bed event CG, its removal, and erotic content with no Japanese counterpart in this script.

findings.evidenceJa: 戦いの行方を見極める
findings.governingReading: The hint tells the player to return to the immediately preceding choice and ascertain how the battle turns out.
findings.explanation: See through the whole battle is unnatural and can mean completing it rather than judging its course at the choice.

findings.governingReading: Taiga says she took Leysritt for taciturn or unsociable before discovering that she understands the situation.
findings.explanation: Blunt changes Leysritt’s sparse manner into rude directness.

findings.governingReading: Leysritt calls the stamp “Tiger” in German, cueing Taiga’s mixed German-Japanese response.
findings.explanation: Translating the cue as ordinary English Tiger hides why Taiga answers with danke and weakens the two-line multilingual joke.
